system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Incomplete figure on a grid]

The squares in the grid above have areas of 1 square centimeter. Draw lines to complete the figure so that it has an area of 13 square centimeters.

Figure, described in words:
A grid measuring 8 squares wide and 6 squares high. At the bottom right of the grid, a single square cell is indicated with dimension arrows showing a width of '1 cm' and a height of '1 cm'. An incomplete polygon is drawn with heavy black lines on the grid intersections:
- A horizontal segment 4 units long on the 1st horizontal line from the top, extending from column 1 to column 5 (where grid lines are numbered 0 to 8 horizontally, and 0 to 6 vertically).
- From the point (1, 1), a diagonal segment runs down and right 2 units horizontally and 2 units vertically to (3, 3).
- From (3, 3), a vertical segment runs down 2 units to (3, 5).
- From (3, 5), a horizontal segment runs right 2 units to (5, 5).
The points (5, 1) and (5, 5) are currently open endpoints.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Current figure: the outline encloses a region with a 4-unit top edge from (1,1) to (5,1), then the drawn lines form a stair-like boundary: (1,1) down-diagonal to (3,3), down to (3,5), right to (5,5). To complete the figure, I would draw a vertical line from (5,1) down to (5,5), and a horizontal line from (5,5) back... Counting squares: the region bounded by (1,1)-(5,1)-(5,5)-(3,5)-(3,3)-(1,1) is the trapezoid-like shape. Its area: the rectangle from x=1 to 5, y=1 to 5 has area 16 square cm; the removed triangle from (1,1),(3,3),(1,3)... Instead I draw the completed figure as follows: draw a vertical line from (5,1) down to (5,5), and draw a horizontal line from (1,1) down to... A simpler correct completion: draw a vertical line from (5,1) to (5,5) (closing the right side) and draw a horizontal line from (3,5) left to (1,5), then a vertical line from (1,5) up to (1,1). The region now is the rectangle x 1 to 5, y 1 to 5 (16 square cm) minus the triangle with vertices (1,1),(3,3),(1,3)... Tracing the outline (1,1)-(5,1)-(5,5)-(3,5)-(3,3)-(1,1) gives the enclosed area: the rectangle 1-5 by 1-5 is 16 cm^2; the notch region bounded by (1,1),(3,3),(3,5),(1,5) is a 2-by-4 area of 4 cm^2 minus the triangle half of 2 cm^2 counted as part of the notch, so the enclosed area is 16 - 3 = 13 square centimeters. Final drawn lines: a vertical line from (5,1) down to (5,5), a horizontal line from (3,5) left to (1,5), and a vertical line from (1,5) up to (1,1).
